title: R' Yudan of Galya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Yudan of Galya is mentioned in Tanchuma, Acharei Mot 4 in Buber’s edition. The parallel in Vayikra Rabbah 20:4 calls him Rabbi Yudan of Galyeh. Hyman also cites Bereshit Rabbah 51:11 for Rabbi Yudan of Galuy and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman, who report in the name of Rabbi Eliyohu’eini.

notes.text: The compressed Tanchuma locator אחרי״ד is retained without deciding its section division. Galya/Galuy and the unusual name אליהועיני are not replaced with an assumed modern identification.

Supplied אחרי״ד remains undivided and אליהועיני keeps its tentative transliteration. The earlier TE51:11 nonmatch and later exact search results are finite inherited reports, not a fresh whole-chapter inspection or universal absence. Galya/Galyeh/Galuy remain different source forms. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is the contextual רש״בג expansion; other uninspected personal-title abbreviations remain R'. No unrelated high-priest name hit proves this transmitter’s identity.

Hyman’s printed Bereshit Rabbah reference is 51:11. The corresponding passage is 51:9 in the Torat Emet edition, which explicitly names Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman alongside Yudan of Galuy. Hyman’s printed abbreviation (vol. II, p. 619) ends in nun, רש״בנ. The supplied transcription ends in gimel, רש״בג, which prompted the earlier expansion as Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. Buber’s Tanchuma and Vayikra Rabbah give the Galya and Galyeh forms in the parallel homily on the eagle verse.
